newsitem.title: UK: Shell confirms interest in Russian Rosneft.
newsitem.headline: Shell confirms interest in Russian Rosneft.

text.p: The Royal Dutch/Shell group confirmed on Tuesday that it was interested in investing in Russia's state-owned oil giant Rosneft.
But a spokesman for the Anglo-Dutch concern declined to comment on the status of discussions or what stake Shell might seek to acquire.
"We are looking at investment opportunities with the larger Russian integrated oil companies which are scheduled for privatisation," the spokesman said in response to inquiries.
"We already have a relationship with Rosneft through the Caspian Pipeline Company (CPC) and we would be interested in building upon this contact."
A Rosneft official said on Monday that both Shell and Exxon had been talking to the Russian company, one of the last large, state energy firms due to be privatised.
Exxon officials were not immediately available for comment.
The privatisation of 51 percent of Rosneft, expected in September, could earn the Russian government some $1 billion.

Shell last year formed a joint venture with the state oil concern to jointly take a 7.5 percent stake in CPC, the $2 billion crude pipeline linking Kazakhstan's Tengiz oilfield to Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
